title: King Joseph to Napoleon, December 1812 (catalogued as Berthier to Napoleon, 22 Dec 1812)

documents.shelfmark: Archives nationales AF/IV/1643 plaquette 1/VI (probable, from the répertoire); printed by Vilcoq 1969

plaintext.source: No clear copy of this letter found. Joseph's letter to the Minister of War of 23 Dec 1812 (Du Casse, Memoires et correspondance du roi Joseph, IX, 1854) covers the same matter in the same phrases; Chuquet's Berthier letters (1912) are a different text.

transcription.source: Vilcoq 1969, plate after p. 24 (Persee), page 3 of the dispatch; re-read by Brice Dudout, 8 groups corrected against the online transcription
transcription.notes: Printed plate of the duplicate (page 3). The first 22 lines are all that is published; the rest of the letter is not.

system.summary: Numeric code of about 1200 groups (2-1388): the Grand Chiffre of 1812, whose deciphering table is at the SHD (B n. 30). Several numbers per frequent word (de = 13, 544, 710, 989, 1060); syllables and letters for the rest.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's Berthier cipher of May 1813 (et = 197, 413, 534, 821) noted, not applied.
system.notes: Marmont 1807 letter not in hand (no ciphertext published), so no document entry; it is a different cipher and has no page. Sibling letters read with the same table: marmont1812.

prior_solution.where: Ilia Chirtulov found that the Great Cipher of 1812 reads it and that the writer is King Joseph (received by S. Tomokiyo 4 Oct 2026, reported on Cryptiana 12 Oct 2026); Brice Dudout's re-reading was independent of it.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded. Second phase (Brice Dudout, 12 Oct 2026): chose the key, froze the table entries, re-read the plate and set the control; Claude (Anthropic) agents helped with the decoding and write-up; model versions not recorded.

solution.what: 325 groups, 207 distinct, 64 % hapax, flat occupancy over about 1200 entries: no frequency signal.
Archives nationales répertoire places the letters in AF/IV/1643; Chuquet 1912 prints them in clear from that carton.
Hapax and distinct-count comparison with Chuquet's letter XXIII; consistent, no alignment proposed.
Vilcoq 1969 (full ciphertext) and Napoleon's reply of 30 Dec 1812 sought online; not reachable.

Tant's ARCSI tables of Imperial great ciphers tried first: unrelated words. The Great Cipher of 1812 (SHD B n. 30, photographs by J.-F. Bouchaudy) read from the first line: 918 je, 1045 n, 1100 ait, 493 aucun, 359 nouvelles ...; the Spanish additions fit (1202 Valladolid, 1238 l'armee du nord de l'Espagne, 1388 Salamanque).

Plate re-read on Persee's high-resolution image: 8 groups differ from the online transcription, each correction makes the passage clear; the 356/656 variant settled (the plate reads 356, the sense requires 656).

French 4-gram score of the decode -2.11 per character against -2.63 median and -2.43 best for 1,000 decodings with the table's values shuffled (0 of 1,000 reach it); model trained on Chuquet's Berthier letters.
Line-by-line French reading and English translation: a letter of King Joseph to the Emperor, not Berthier's; cross-checked against Joseph's letter to the Minister of War of 23 Dec 1812 (Du Casse IX).
Count by the 95% rule: 233 words, 225 certain, 3 probable, 5 restored from the sense, 0 unresolved.

outcome.method_basis: The deciphering table of the Great Cipher of 1812 (SHD B n. 30, photographs by J.-F. Bouchaudy) applied unchanged to the 325 printed groups; the decode builds French sentences, and a permutation control (0 of 1,000 shuffled tables reach its score) and the sister letter of 23 Dec 1812 confirm it.
outcome.notes: Catalogued by Tomokiyo as Berthier to Napoleon; the writer is King Joseph. Only the printed page is available; the unpublished rest needs the Archives nationales original.

texts.label: King Joseph to Napoleon, Spain, December 1812 (the 325 printed groups, page 3 of the dispatch)
texts.summary: King Joseph, with no news from the Emperor since he left Paris, reports that his last courier was seized near Valladolid, encloses General Reille's dispatch on the Army of the North and, shaken by it, begins to propose a remedy for the concentration of forces if the Russian war continues. The letter was filed as a duplicate in Berthier's name; its text breaks off at the end of page 3.

reading_review.note: reading.md and translation.md read against decryption.txt: the 22 lines build coherent French sentences with no sentence broken; the 5 restored groups are scattered and each sits in a word whose sense is fixed (reiterees, concentration, exigeat). Not checked against the plate sign by sign.
